message.content:
This appears to be a CBP ruling on an EVinsulate panel, a polycarbonate panel for the Tesla Model Y glass roof. The key question is whether it is a vehicle part (Chapter 87) or a plastic article (Chapter 39).

The panel is an aftermarket insulating panel attached under the glass roof. Section XVII, Note 2 excludes parts that are general-purpose articles of Section XV and similar goods of plastics (Chapter 39). Chapter 39 therefore needs a closer look. Heading 3926 covers other articles of plastics, including 3926.30 for fittings for furniture, coachwork and the like. Heading 3926.90 is the residual. Heading 3920 covers plates, sheets and film of plastics, non-cellular, not reinforced, unworked or merely surface-worked or cut into squares or rectangles. This panel is cut to a specific shape and bent, so it falls outside 3920.

Heading 8708 covers parts and accessories of motor vehicles. Because Note 2(l) to Section XVII excludes goods of Chapter 39 as a class, the Chapter 39 route is likely. Note 2(l) to Section XVII excludes "articles of chapter 39"? Section XVII Note 2 does not list all Chapter 39 articles. It excludes only parts of general use under Note 2 of Section XV, and the items in 2(a) through 2(f), which do not include Chapter 39 generally. So 8708.99 would be possible. However, I recall that CBP classified a similar panel under 8708.29.5160 as "other parts and accessories of bodies," and those rulings concerned USMCA eligibility. Another candidate is 8708.99.8180.

I will go with 8708.29.5160, which covers other parts and accessories of bodies (including cab) in the 8708.29 subheading. The roof panel counts as a body part.

{"hts_code": "8708.29.5160", "reason": "The cut and bent polycarbonate panel is an aftermarket accessory fitted to the glass roof of a Tesla Model Y, so it is classified as an other part or accessory of motor vehicle bodies in heading 8708."}
